- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to be overly optimistic in the middle of the horizon (days 10–20), underestimating subsequent corrections.
- Model underreacts to strong downward trends in recent history — fails to adjust forecast downward when true outcome shows sharp declines.
- When true outcome shows a clear mean-reverting pattern, model continues to trend upward or fails to recognize the reversal.
- Model often ignores short-term volatility and reacts slowly to sudden price drops or spikes — lagging by 1–3 days in adjustment.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true outcome — underestimates volatility and overestimates stability, especially in the last 5–10 days.
